hero.title: Book & Journal Typesetting Services
hero.lead: Professional page composition and layout production for book publishers, academic publishers and journal publishing teams.
paragraphs: Book and journal page composition for publishers, including complex tables, figures, equations and references, prepared to the approved layout and delivery specifications.

sections.title: Typesetting for Books, Journals & Academic Publications

lead.text: Different publication types require different approaches to page composition. EPUBTRANS supports typesetting requirements based on the structure, complexity and intended use of the content.

blocks.text: We support publishers with book page composition and formatting according to supplied designs, templates and publishing specifications.
Book typesetting can be scoped for text-led publications or more complex layouts involving numerous visual and structural elements.
Academic and scholarly journals often require consistent article layouts, references, figures, tables and publication-specific formatting.
The production scope may include article headings, author information, abstracts, body text, mathematical content, citations, references, captions and related publication elements.
Where journals use established templates or design specifications, these can guide the production workflow.
Academic and technical publications may contain mathematical equations, scientific symbols, complex tables, figures and multiple levels of headings.
We assess the complexity of the supplied material and clarify any specialist formatting requirements before confirming the production approach.

lead.text: Typesetting involves more than placing manuscript text into pages. It requires organizing content according to a defined typographic and layout structure.

blocks.text: Preparation of publication pages using the supplied design specifications, page dimensions, templates and formatting requirements.
Activities may include managing margins, columns, text flow, page breaks and the positioning of publication elements.
Application of consistent text styles throughout the publication, including heading hierarchies, body text, captions, quotations, footnotes and other content elements.
Typography requirements may include font selection or application, line spacing, paragraph spacing, alignment and hyphenation according to the approved design.
Formatting and placement of tables, charts, illustrations, equations and other technical elements within the page layout.
The work depends on source quality, complexity, available artwork and the publisher's requirements.
Formatting of tables of contents, bibliographies, reference lists, footnotes, endnotes, running heads, page numbers and other publication elements.
The creation or substantive editing of references is separate from their visual formatting unless explicitly included in the project.
Application of approved author or publisher corrections to typeset pages.
Correction rounds, revision limits, responsibility for content changes and final approval stages are defined during project scoping.

lead.text: Providing complete source materials and production instructions helps clarify the scope and reduce avoidable production queries.
The final deliverables depend on the publication type, source files and agreed production requirements.

blocks.text: Depending on the publication, useful materials may include:

items: Manuscript files, preferably in an editable format
Publisher style sheets or design specifications
Existing templates or reference publication samples
Page size, margins and layout instructions
Font files or approved font specifications, where applicable
Instructions for references, footnotes, indexes and other publication elements
Required proof format and final delivery specifications

blocks.text: If some materials are unavailable, we can review the information provided and identify what is needed before production begins.
PDF proofs or other agreed review files for checking page composition and incorporating approved corrections.
PDF files prepared against the agreed print or digital publishing specifications.
Print-ready file preparation and printer-specific checks are included only when defined in the project scope.
Native layout files and associated production assets in agreed formats, where required and supported.
Related layout resources and agreed supporting files needed for the client's downstream publishing workflow.
The exact file formats, versions, packaging and delivery requirements are confirmed before production.
We examine the manuscript, design references, publication requirements and available supporting assets.
During this stage, we identify structural or formatting complexities that may affect production.
Where the project requires it, we prepare or adapt the page layout based on the approved design specifications.
A sample or representative pages may be prepared for review when included in the production process.
The manuscript is formatted and composed according to the agreed layout, content structure and publication specifications.
Tables, figures, references and other content elements are incorporated as required.
Relevant visual, layout and content-presentation checks are performed according to the project scope.
Approved corrections and revision requests are incorporated through the agreed review process.
After the required reviews and approvals, final files are prepared in the agreed formats and delivery structure.

lead.text: Typesetting quality depends on how accurately the prepared pages follow the required publication specifications.
Depending on the project, quality checks may cover:

items: Consistency of text styles and heading levels
Running heads, footers and page numbering
Text overflow, missing content and unexpected page breaks
Visual comparison with an approved design or reference
Final file structure and delivery requirements

lead.text: Quality checks are performed according to the agreed scope. Copyediting, language proofreading, independent technical validation and printer-specific preflight are not automatically included in a typesetting assignment.
The effort required for a publication depends on several factors.

blocks.text: A text-only manuscript typically presents different requirements from an illustrated textbook or a technical journal article containing extensive equations, tables and figures.
Well-structured editable manuscripts are generally easier to prepare than inconsistent, incomplete or non-editable source files.
Publisher-specific templates, page dimensions, typographic standards and complex page structures affect the production approach.
The number and nature of review stages, author corrections and changes after pagination can influence the work required.
A project requiring page proofs and final PDFs may have a different scope from one requiring editable production files, additional formats or downstream publishing preparation.
We review these requirements before defining the production scope and preparing an estimate.

lead.text: Typesetting is one part of the wider publishing-production workflow. Depending on your requirements, related EPUBTRANS services may include:

blocks.text: Editorial preparation and language consistency work before typesetting, where required.
Review of prepared content or publication proofs within an agreed proofreading scope.
EPUB creation and eBook conversion for publications intended for digital reading environments.
Structured-content preparation for applicable academic and journal publishing workflows.
Preparation or refinement of publication graphics and visual assets.
These services can be discussed separately or assessed as part of a broader production requirement.

groups.title: What types of publications can EPUBTRANS typeset?

blocks.text: Our documented service scope includes book and journal typesetting. We can assess academic, technical and other publication requirements based on the manuscript, content complexity and expected outputs.

groups.title: Can you work with manuscripts supplied in Microsoft Word?

blocks.text: Word manuscripts are among the documented input types for publishing production. We review their structure, formatting and supporting assets before confirming the production approach.

groups.title: Can you typeset books or journals containing equations, tables and figures?

blocks.text: These elements are part of the documented typesetting scope. Their complexity, source format and required presentation are assessed during project planning.

groups.title: Do you provide print-ready PDF files?

blocks.text: Print-ready PDF preparation may be included where specified. Printer requirements, final proof approval and any preflight checks should be confirmed before production.
Not automatically. Typesetting focuses on page composition and formatting. Editorial proofreading can be included as a separately agreed service.

groups.title: Can you follow our existing publisher design or journal template?

blocks.text: Publisher design references, style sheets and layout templates can be used to define the required page composition. Please provide the relevant materials for review.

groups.title: Can we request corrections after receiving typeset proofs?

blocks.text: Correction rounds can be included in the agreed workflow. The number of review stages, permitted changes and responsibilities should be established before production.

groups.title: What information do you need to prepare a quote?

blocks.text: A representative manuscript, approximate page or word count, publication type, sample pages, formatting instructions, expected deliverables and preferred schedule help us assess your requirements.

lead.text: Looking for book, journal or academic publishing typesetting support?
Share your manuscript details, publication specifications, approximate volume and expected deliverables.
EPUBTRANS can review the information and discuss a suitable production approach for your project.
